# Deep Research Intelligence Packet

## Cycle metadata

- Packet ID: `dr-20260929-1605-alchemer-validation`
- Research system: `Codex web research`
- Started at: `2026-09-29 16:05 CDT`
- Completed at: `2026-09-29 16:09 CDT`
- Research scope: Validate four first-party Alchemer pages for named restaurant deployments, product scope, operating use, and outcome limitations.
- Queue item or vendor: `competitor:alchemer`
- Methodology: First-party customer-page validation with product-lineage, deployment-scope, outcome-causality, and recency boundaries preserved.

## Executive result

- Pages reviewed: 4
- Candidate pages validated: 4
- Brand-vendor-product observations added or revised: 5
- Company/competitor profile observations added or revised: 1
- Conflicts found: 3
- Material takeaway: Alchemer publishes named restaurant evidence across mobile app feedback, reputation/listings management, AI review signals, sentiment analysis, and operational reporting. Dunkin', A&W, Paris Baguette, True Food Kitchen, and Figaro's/Pizza Schmizza are supported as customers or active users, but the outcome figures are vendor-authored and product naming spans acquired products formerly called Apptentive and Chatmeter.

## Evidence observations

### Observation 1

- Brand: Dunkin'
- Vendor: Alchemer
- Product or category: Alchemer Mobile, formerly Apptentive; in-app surveys, Love Dialog, Mobile Notes, ratings and reviews, and mobile sentiment
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: enterprise
- Evidence type: customer story
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Alchemer's named customer story includes a quote from Dunkin' Brands' Senior Product Manager, product-level usage details, and quantified vendor-reported outcomes.
- Source title: The Dunkin'-Alchemer Mobile Success Story
- Source URL: https://www.alchemer.com/mobile/dunkin/
- Publisher or source owner: Alchemer
- Published date, if known: Undated
- Accessed date: 2026-09-29
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Dunkin' uses Alchemer Mobile surveys, Love Dialog, and Mobile Notes to prioritize app changes, read sentiment after releases, and communicate promotions; Alchemer reports a 20% survey response rate, a star-rating increase from 2.0 to 4.5, and 74% positive Love Dialog responses.
- Product-specific evidence: In-app surveys identified requests for donut-sprinkle and iced-coffee ice options; Mobile Notes supported fast mass communication around National Coffee Day.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page is vendor-authored and undated. The 631.4K monthly-download figure describes app scale, not the number of users exposed to Alchemer. The outcome metrics lack measurement windows and independent validation.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm current SDK/product use and measurement windows from a Dunkin-controlled privacy, app-release, procurement, or technical source.

### Observation 2

- Brand: A&W Restaurants
- Vendor: Alchemer, formerly Chatmeter
- Product or category: Listings management, review management, local SEO, competitive measurement, and review response
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: enterprise
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 90%
- Confidence rationale: The named case study quotes an A&W spokesperson, describes use in franchise-opening scorecards, and provides product and operating details across franchised locations.
- Source title: See how A&W captures 25% increase in 5-star reviews on Google in six months
- Source URL: https://www.alchemer.com/resources/case-study/a-w/
- Publisher or source owner: Alchemer
- Published date, if known: Undated
- Accessed date: 2026-09-29
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: A&W uses Alchemer reviews, platform participation, and manager training in the scorecard for proposed new franchise locations; the platform supports listings accuracy, review monitoring and response, local SEO, and location-level operational insight.
- Product-specific evidence: Vendor-reported results include higher Google and Yelp page-one appearances, click-to-call actions, five-star reviews, listings accuracy, and review-response rates after deployment.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page uses the current Alchemer name for a deployment formerly branded Chatmeter. Quantified outcomes are vendor-authored and are not accompanied by raw baselines, dates, or independent attribution.
- Recommended follow-up: Seek A&W-controlled franchise documentation or current privacy/procurement evidence and confirm whether the legacy Chatmeter deployment remains active across the full estate.

### Observation 3

- Brand: Paris Baguette
- Vendor: Alchemer
- Product or category: Review aggregation, surveys, listings management, sentiment analysis, competitive benchmarking, NPS/CSAT, Pulse AI, and AI Review Signals
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: regional
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Alchemer's named case study quotes Paris Baguette's Ops Service Analyst and supplies concrete cross-location workflows and operational examples across more than 300 U.S. and Canadian cafés.
- Source title: From feedback to operational action: How Paris Baguette scales guest experience across hundreds of franchise cafés
- Source URL: https://www.alchemer.com/resources/case-study/how-paris-baguette-turns-customer-feedback-into-operational-action-across-300-franchise-locations/
- Publisher or source owner: Alchemer
- Published date, if known: Undated
- Accessed date: 2026-09-29
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Paris Baguette centralizes reviews, surveys, listings, sentiment, and competitive benchmarks in Alchemer for weekly reporting and franchise coaching across more than 300 U.S. and Canadian cafés.
- Product-specific evidence: The case study reports 98% listings accuracy, more than 146,000 feedback items over five years, Google-rating movement from 4.2 to 4.4, detection of supplier quality and training issues, and AI Review Signals that helped identify drink-temperature and online-order accuracy problems.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page is vendor-authored; scale and outcome metrics are not independently audited. The case study shows regional North American scope, not a global enterprise deployment, and correlation does not isolate Alchemer as the sole cause of rating changes.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm the deployment and metrics in Paris Baguette-controlled operations or franchise materials and identify any connected POS, loyalty, or ordering integrations.

### Observation 4

- Brand: True Food Kitchen
- Vendor: Alchemer
- Product or category: Review sentiment tagging, feedback reporting, and location/brand performance measurement
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: enterprise
- Evidence type: customer story
- Confidence: 90%
- Confidence rationale: Alchemer's dated article names a True Food Kitchen analyst, explains the internal operating cadence, and links a specific sentiment signal to a seven-week menu reversal.
- Source title: How True Food Kitchen, Figaro's, and Pizza Schmizza turned diner feedback into operational change
- Source URL: https://www.alchemer.com/resources/blog/how-true-food-kitchen-figaros-and-pizza-schmizza-turned-diner-feedback-into-operational-change/
- Publisher or source owner: Alchemer
- Published date, if known: 2026-08-11; updated 2026-09-18
- Accessed date: 2026-09-29
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: True Food Kitchen uses Alchemer sentiment tags and a weekly reporting cadence across its 45 restaurants; a sharp negative-sentiment spike after removal of a longstanding chopped salad informed its return seven weeks later.
- Product-specific evidence: Review and sentiment reporting flows from a Wednesday report to Friday regional calls and a Tuesday operator newsletter; sentiment scoring is also tied to location performance and quarterly incentives.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The source is vendor-authored and does not establish that sentiment analysis alone caused the menu decision or disclose the full technical stack, contract term, or implementation date.
- Recommended follow-up: Seek True Food Kitchen-controlled confirmation and identify the review sources, integrations, and governance around employee incentives.

### Observation 5

- Brand: Figaro's Pizza and Pizza Schmizza
- Vendor: Alchemer
- Product or category: Review aggregation, operational feedback analysis, customer-lifetime-value framing, and AI-assisted review responses
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: enterprise
- Evidence type: customer story
- Confidence: 90%
- Confidence rationale: The dated Alchemer article quotes the brands' Marketing Director and describes specific implemented uses and a current AI-response pilot across an approximately 50-franchisee system.
- Source title: How True Food Kitchen, Figaro's, and Pizza Schmizza turned diner feedback into operational change
- Source URL: https://www.alchemer.com/resources/blog/how-true-food-kitchen-figaros-and-pizza-schmizza-turned-diner-feedback-into-operational-change/
- Publisher or source owner: Alchemer
- Published date, if known: 2026-08-11; updated 2026-09-18
- Accessed date: 2026-09-29
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Review patterns in Alchemer helped the brands identify a location-level oven-temperature problem and allergy concerns that informed a gluten-free crust; the team is piloting AI-generated review responses in brand voice.
- Product-specific evidence: Review monitoring, response workflows, operational issue detection, feedback-to-menu decisions, and AI-assisted responses.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The AI-generated response capability is a pilot, not a completed estate-wide rollout. The source does not separate Figaro's and Pizza Schmizza deployment counts or independently validate operational outcomes.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm pilot scope, current rollout status, and whether both brands use the same tenant, workflows, and integrations.

## Company / competitor profile observations

### Company profile observation 1

- Target: `competitor:alchemer`
- Field: `product_lineage`
- Value or observation: Alchemer's restaurant-facing portfolio includes capabilities formerly branded Apptentive for mobile experience and Chatmeter for listings/reputation management, alongside current Alchemer products such as Pulse AI and AI Review Signals; source-level product lineage should be retained when comparing deployments.
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Alchemer's own Dunkin' and A&W pages explicitly label the respective products as formerly Apptentive and formerly Chatmeter, while the Paris Baguette case study uses current Pulse AI and AI Review Signals naming.
- Source title: The Dunkin'-Alchemer Mobile Success Story; A&W case study; Paris Baguette case study
- Source URL: https://www.alchemer.com/mobile/dunkin/
- Publisher or source owner: Alchemer
- Published date, if known: Undated
- Accessed date: 2026-09-29
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The Dunkin' page says Alchemer Mobile was formerly Apptentive; the A&W page says Alchemer was formerly Chatmeter; current Paris Baguette materials name Pulse AI and AI Review Signals.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The pages establish brand lineage but do not disclose migration dates, contract continuity, data migration, or whether all legacy customers use the full current platform.

## Negative findings

- Candidate or claim: The named restaurant deployments prove Alchemer is a core POS, payments, ordering, or loyalty-system vendor.
- Pages checked: Dunkin', A&W, Paris Baguette, and the joint True Food Kitchen/Figaro's/Pizza Schmizza article.
- Result: The pages support customer-feedback, digital-experience, reputation/listings, sentiment, and operational-insight use cases. They do not establish Alchemer as the system of record for POS, payments, ordering, or loyalty.

## Source ledger

| URL | Source type | Accessed | Supports observation(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| https://www.alchemer.com/mobile/dunkin/ | Customer story | 2026-09-29 | 1; profile 1 | Named Alchemer Mobile deployment; undated and metrics are vendor-reported. |
| https://www.alchemer.com/resources/case-study/a-w/ | Case study | 2026-09-29 | 2; profile 1 | Named former-Chatmeter deployment with franchise scorecard and review/listings use; current estate scope not independently verified. |
| https://www.alchemer.com/resources/case-study/how-paris-baguette-turns-customer-feedback-into-operational-action-across-300-franchise-locations/ | Case study | 2026-09-29 | 3; profile 1 | Named North American deployment across 300+ cafés with current product names and detailed workflows. |
| https://www.alchemer.com/resources/blog/how-true-food-kitchen-figaros-and-pizza-schmizza-turned-diner-feedback-into-operational-change/ | Customer story | 2026-09-29 | 4, 5 | Dated joint story with named operators and concrete actions; AI response use remains a pilot. |

## Research notes and inferences

- Inference: Alchemer competes most directly in restaurant feedback intelligence, reputation/listings, and digital-experience measurement rather than as a transaction system.
- Inference: Its acquired product lineage broadens restaurant coverage but creates a verification need: legacy customer evidence should not automatically be treated as adoption of every current Alchemer module.
- Review instruction: Preserve vendor-authored outcome metrics as reported evidence, not independently verified causality, and keep pilots distinct from completed rollouts.
